The checked core WASM fixture is compiled from `component-guest` with generated
WIT bindings. Normal host tests package it through `wit-component` and execute
it through the production actor; they require no WASM compiler and are never
silently skipped. The fixture covers real Rust allocation, Unicode, state,
resource destructors, staged effects, and deliberate faults.

`sdk-guest.wasm` additionally compiles the public Rust SDK and its export macro,
then exercises the ergonomic metadata/read and UI response adapter in normal
runtime tests. Both Rust fixtures are regenerated by the same script.

After WIT or fixture-source changes, run `regenerate.sh --offline`. CI can rebuild
with the pinned Rust toolchain and compare the artifact. The independent fixture
workspace has its own lockfile and target directory, so regeneration never
changes the editor's dependency lock. The binary is source WASM, never a native
serialized engine artifact.

The second checked core fixture, `c-guest.wasm`, uses C bindings generated from
the same production WIT by wit-bindgen 0.62.0. `regenerate-c.sh --offline` needs
Clang with a wasm32 target and `wasm-ld`; its build tools use the separate locked
benchmark workspace. `MITOS_C_BINDINGS` may point to an already built generator.
The freestanding allocator in `c-guest/guest.c` belongs to this small test only.
The normal C smoke test checks repeated resource destruction, scoped Unicode
reads, and staged edits without a C toolchain or WASI in the host test process.

`router-guest` is a configurable public-SDK guest shared by editor and terminal
regressions. Its checked packaged component executes route metadata checks,
ordering guards, revisioned reads, Unicode transformations, and intentional
faults through the real component host. Expected fragments are checked against
a request with fixture configuration removed, so assertions cannot accidentally
match themselves. The same regeneration script rebuilds and packages it.
